sections.text_helper: Section 24.4.11 "OPAMP calibration" in chapter 24 (Operational amplifier (OPAMP)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 737.
sections.section_content:
The calibration allows finding the trimming values that minimize the operational amplifier
offset.
Setting the CALON bit isolates the operational amplifier INP and INM inputs and connects
them to the internal reference voltage level selected through the CALSEL[1:0] bitfield. The
operational amplifier is in a comparator (high gain, open loop) mode in which its output
transits from one rail to another when the voltage level on one input crosses the voltage
level on the other input.
The CALOUT flag reflects this digital value (lower rail or upper rail) of the OPAMP_VOUT
pin.
The CALSEL[1:0] bitfield values 01 (low reference voltage) and 11 (high reference voltage)
are intended for use in the calibration procedure. The value 01 is for trimming the PMOS
through the TRIMOFFSETP[4:0] bitfield, the value 11 for trimming the NMOS through the
TRIMOFFSETN[4:0] bitfield.
The calibration is carried out by software. Starting from the trimming bitfield at 0 and the
CALOUT flag at one, the procedure consists in incrementing the trimming value until the
CALOUT flag toggles to 0. The last trimming value is the one that compensates for the
operational amplifier offset of the given OPAMP instance, and for the given supply voltage,
die temperature, and differential pair stage (PMOS or NMOS). Upon each trimming value
incrementation, the software must wait for at least the tOFFTRIMmax period defined in the
product datasheet, before reading the CALOUT flag and potentially proceeding to the next
incrementation step.
Note: The closer is the trimming value to the offset compensation point, the longer the output
voltage takes to respond (without ever exceeding tOFFTRIMmax).
The full calibration consists of four calibration loops, as listed in Table182. They can be
executed in any order. The CALON bit must be set for executing any calibration loop. The
calibration loops for the operational amplifier speed (slew rate) not required in the
application can be omitted.
[Table 182. Calibrationloops]
Different OPAMP instances can be calibrated at any time, even at the same time.
Calibration initialization
To initialize the offset trimming value calibration:
• Enable OPAMP, by setting OPAEN.
• Make the trimming bitfields writable, by setting USERTRIM.
• Write TRIMOFFSETN[4:0] and TRIMOFFSETP[4:0] bitfields with 0b00000.
Calibration loop sequence
To execute a calibration loop, go through the following steps:
1. Select the calibration loop, with the CALSEL[1:0] bitfield. That is, the speed (slew rate)
and the differential pair end (NMOS or PMOS) to calibrate.
2. Increment the appropriate trimming bitfield (TRIMOFFSETN[4:0] for NMOS,
TRIMOFFSETP[4:0] for PMOS), keeping the other trimming bitfield as is.
3. Wait for at least the tOFFTRIMmax period.
4. Check the CALOUT flag (OPAINTOEN=0). If high, go to step 2 (loop back).
5. The trimming bitfield is calibrated. Store the calibrated trimming value if required.
For a given speed (slew rate), execute both the NMOS and the PMOS calibration loops.
Note: During the calibration loop execution, the external connection of the operational amplifier
output must not pull up or down currents exceeding 500µA.
Calibrating when operational amplifier output goes to a COMP input
With the operational amplifier output redirected to an internal COMP input channel
(OPAINTOEN bit set), the CALOUT flag does not reflect the operational amplifier output. To
address this, it is advised to clear the OPAINTOEN bit for the time of calibration to make the
CALOUT flag operate. When the calibration is completed, set OPAINTOEN to redirect the
operational amplifier output back to a COMP input channel. As during the calibration the
internal signal sent to the OPAMP_VOUT pin toggles, take care to prevent any conflict on
the pin. For example, use the pin in the application as an input.
